sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā svanavantaṃ mahādhvajam rathaṃ rākṣasarājasya nararājo dadarśa ha
english: The king among men beheld the chariot of the king of the rākṣasas rushing forward suddenly, resounding loudly, bearing great banners.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇavājisamāyuktaṃ yuktaṃ raudreṇa varcasā taḍitpatākāgahanaṃ darśitendrāyudhāyudham śaradhārā vimuñcantaṃ dhārāsāram ivānbudam
english: Yoked with dark horses, endowed with a fierce radiance, thick with banners like lightning-flashes, displaying weapons like Indra's own rainbow-bow, it poured streams of arrows like a cloud discharging a torrent of rain.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā meghasaṃkāśam āpatantaṃ rathaṃ ripoḥ girer vajrābhimṛṣṭasya dīryataḥ sadṛśasvanam uvāca mātaliṃ rāmaḥ sahasrākṣasya sārathim
english: Seeing the chariot of his enemy rushing forward, resembling a storm-cloud, with a sound like that of a mountain cleaving under the thunderbolt's stroke, Rāma spoke to Mātali, charioteer of the thousand-eyed Indra.

sanskrit: mātale paśya saṃrabdham āpatantaṃ rathaṃ ripoḥ yathāpasavyaṃ patatā vegena mahatā punaḥ samare hantum ātmānaṃ tathānena kṛtā matiḥ
english: "Mātali, see the chariot of the foe rushing forward in great fury — by coming at such tremendous speed from the inauspicious side, he has resolved, it seems, to destroy himself in battle."

sanskrit: tad apramādam ātiṣṭha pratyudgaccha rathaṃ ripoḥ vidhvaṃsayitum icchāmi vāyur megham ivotthitam
english: "Therefore be alert; advance to meet the foe's chariot. I wish to scatter it as the wind scatters a risen cloud."

sanskrit: aviklavam asaṃbhrāntam avyagrahṛdayekṣaṇam raśmisaṃcāraniyataṃ pracodaya rathaṃ drutam
english: "Without hesitation, without confusion, with heart and eyes undistracted, keeping firm hold of the reins, drive the chariot swiftly."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ na tvaṃ samādheyaḥ puraṃdararathocitaḥ yuyutsur aham ekāgraḥ smāraye tvāṃ na śikṣaye
english: "You who are accustomed to Indra's chariot need not be instructed; I, bent solely on battle, only remind you — I do not teach you."

sanskrit: parituṣṭaḥ sa rāmasya tena vākyena mātaliḥ pracodayām āsa rathaṃ surasārathisattamaḥ
english: Pleased by those words of Rāma, Mātali, foremost among the charioteers of the gods, drove the chariot forward.

sanskrit: apasavyaṃ tataḥ kurvan rāvaṇasya mahāratham cakrotkṣiptena rajasā rāvaṇaṃ vyavadhūnayat
english: Then, circling Rāvaṇa's great chariot from the auspicious side and throwing up dust from the wheel, he shook Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho daśagrīvas tāmravisphāritekṣaṇaḥ rathapratimukhaṃ rāmaṃ sāyakair avadhūnayat
english: Then the ten-headed one, enraged, his eyes wide and copper-red, assailed Rāma, who stood facing him in the chariot, with a volley of arrows.

sanskrit: dharṣaṇāmarṣito rāmo dhairyaṃ roṣeṇa laṅghayan jagrāha sumahāvegam aindraṃ yudhi śarāsanam śarāṃś ca sumahātejāḥ sūryaraśmisamaprabhān
english: Rāma, of exceeding splendour, stung with indignation at that assault, his steadiness overpowered by wrath, took up in battle the bow of Indra of immense velocity, along with arrows blazing bright as the sun's rays.

sanskrit: tad upoḍhaṃ mahad yuddham anyonyavadhakāṅkṣiṇoḥ parasparābhimukhayor dṛptayor iva siṃhayoḥ
english: Then a great battle was joined between those two, each eager to slay the other, facing one another like two proud lions.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ samīyur dvairathaṃ draṣṭuṃ rāvaṇakṣayakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Then the gods together with the Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the great seers assembled to witness the chariot-duel, all longing for Rāvaṇa's destruction.

sanskrit: samutpetur athotpātā dāruṇā lomaharṣaṇāḥ rāvaṇasya vināśāya rāghavasya jayāya ca
english: Then dreadful and hair-raising portents arose, presaging the destruction of Rāvaṇa and the victory of Rāghava.

sanskrit: vavarṣa rudhiraṃ devo rāvaṇasya rathopari vātā maṇḍalinas tīvrā apasavyaṃ pracakramuḥ
english: The sky rained blood upon Rāvaṇa's chariot; violent whirlwinds circled in the inauspicious direction.

sanskrit: mahad gṛdhrakulaṃ cāsya bhramamāṇaṃ nabhastale yena yena ratho yāti tena tena pradhāvati
english: A great flock of vultures, hovering in the sky, flew in whatever direction his chariot moved.

sanskrit: saṃdhyayā cāvṛtā laṅkā japāpuṣpanikāśayā dṛśyate saṃpradīteva divase 'pi vasuṃdharā
english: Laṅkā was enshrouded in a reddish twilight hue like the hibiscus flower; even by day the earth appeared as if ablaze.

sanskrit: sanirghātā maholkāś ca saṃpracetur mahāsvanāḥ viṣādayantyo rakṣāṃsi rāvaṇasya tadāhitāḥ
english: Enormous meteors accompanied by thunderous crashes fell with great roaring sounds, despairing the rākṣasas and boding ill for Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaś ca yatas tatra pracacāla vasuṃdharā rakṣasāṃ ca praharatāṃ gṛhītā iva bāhavaḥ
english: Wherever Rāvaṇa stood, the earth trembled; and the arms of the striking rākṣasas felt as if seized and held.

sanskrit: tāmrāḥ pītāḥ sitāḥ śvetāḥ patitāḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ dṛśyante rāvaṇasyāṅge parvatasyeva dhātavaḥ
english: Copper-red, yellow, pale, and white rays of the sun fell upon Rāvaṇa's body, appearing like the mineral veins of a mountain.

sanskrit: gṛdhrair anugatāś cāsya vamantyo jvalanaṃ mukhaiḥ praṇedur mukham īkṣantyaḥ saṃrabdham aśivaṃ śivāḥ
english: Followed by vultures and spewing fire from their mouths, jackals shrieked ominously, looking toward his face with fury.

sanskrit: pratikūlaṃ vavau vāyū raṇe pāṃsūn samutkiran tasya rākṣasarājasya kurvan dṛṣṭivilopanam
english: A contrary wind blew in the battle, raising dust and blinding the eyes of that king of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: nipetur indrāśanayaḥ sainye cāsya samantataḥ durviṣahya svanā ghorā vinā jaladharasvanam
english: Indra's thunderbolts fell all around his army with terrible, unbearable sounds, not accompanied by any sound of clouds.

sanskrit: diśaś ca pradiśaś ca sarvā babhūvus timirāvṛtāḥ pāṃsuvarṣeṇa mahatā durdarśaṃ ca nabho 'bhavat
english: All the cardinal and intermediate directions became shrouded in darkness; with a great rain of dust the sky became difficult to see.

sanskrit: kurvantyaḥ kalahaṃ ghoraṃ sārikās tadrathaṃ prati nipetuḥ śataśas tatra dāruṇā dāruṇasvanāḥ
english: Making dreadful quarrelsome cries, hundreds of śārikā birds fell upon his chariot, terrible and uttering terrible sounds.

sanskrit: jaghanebhyaḥ sphuliṅgāṃś ca netrebhyo 'śrūṇi saṃtatam mumucus tasya turagās tulyam agniṃ ca vāri ca
english: His horses shed sparks from their haunches and a constant stream of tears from their eyes — fire and water equally.

sanskrit: evaṃ prakārā bahavaḥ samutpātā bhayāvahāḥ rāvaṇasya vināśāya dāruṇāḥ saṃprajajñire
english: Thus many dreadful and fearful portents of this kind arose for the destruction of Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: rāmasyāpi nimittāni saumyāni ca śivāni ca babhūvur jayaśaṃsīni prādurbhūtāni sarvaśaḥ
english: And for Rāma too, omens that were gentle and auspicious appeared on all sides, proclaiming victory.

sanskrit: tato nirīkṣyātmagatāni rāghavo raṇe nimittāni nimittakovidaḥ jagāma harṣaṃ ca parāṃ ca nirvṛtiṃ cakāra yuddhe 'bhyadhikaṃ ca vikramam
english: Then Rāghava, skilled in reading omens, observing those omens that had come to him, felt supreme joy and delight, and redoubled his valour in battle.
note: Verse 6.94.29 is read as a combined pāda in several recensions.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravṛttaṃ sukrūraṃ rāmarāvaṇayos tadā sumahad dvairathaṃ yuddhaṃ sarvalokabhayāvaham
english: Then there commenced between Rāma and Rāvaṇa a very great chariot-duel, utterly fierce, striking fear into all the worlds.

sanskrit: tato rākṣasasainyaṃ ca harīṇāṃ ca mahad balam pragṛhītapraharaṇaṃ niśceṣṭaṃ samatiṣṭhata
english: Then both the rākṣasa army and the great host of monkeys stood weapons raised yet motionless, transfixed.

sanskrit: saṃprayuddhau tato dṛṣṭvā balavan nararākṣasau vyākṣiptahṛdayāḥ sarve paraṃ vismayam āgatāḥ
english: Seeing those two mighty combatants, the man and the rākṣasa, locked in battle, all were overcome in their hearts and seized with the greatest wonder.

sanskrit: nānāpraharaṇair vyagrair bhujair vismitabuddhayaḥ tasthuḥ prekṣya ca saṃgrāmaṃ nābhijaghnuḥ parasparam
english: With arms busy wielding various weapons, their minds astounded, they stood watching the battle and did not strike one another.

sanskrit: rakṣasāṃ rāvaṇaṃ cāpi vānarāṇāṃ ca rāghavam paśyatāṃ vismitākṣāṇāṃ sainyaṃ citram ivābabhau
english: The army appeared like a painting — the rākṣasas with eyes fixed in wonder upon Rāvaṇa, the monkeys with eyes fixed in wonder upon Rāghava.

sanskrit: tau tu tatra nimittāni dṛṣṭvā rāghavarāvaṇau kṛtabuddhī sthirāmarṣau yuyudhāte abhītavat
english: But those two, Rāghava and Rāvaṇa, having observed the omens and made up their minds, steady in their fury, fought without fear.

sanskrit: jetavyam iti kākutstho martavyam iti rāvaṇaḥ dhṛtau svavīryasarvasvaṃ yuddhe 'darśayatāṃ tadā
english: Kākutstha resolved "I must conquer" and Rāvaṇa resolved "I must die fighting" — both staking the whole of their valour, they displayed it in battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhād daśagrīvaḥ śarān saṃdhāya vīryavān mumoca dhvajam uddiśya rāghavasya rathe sthitam
english: Then the mighty ten-headed one, in anger, fitting arrows to his bow, released them aimed at the standard mounted on Rāghava's chariot.

sanskrit: te śarās tam anāsādya puraṃdararathadhvajam raktaśaktiṃ parāmṛśya nipetur dharaṇītale
english: Those arrows, failing to reach the standard of Indra's chariot, merely grazed the red-painted lance-staff and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tato rāmo 'bhisaṃkruddhaś cāpam āyamya vīryavān kṛtapratikṛtaṃ kartuṃ manasā saṃpracakrame
english: Then Rāma, greatly enraged, the mighty one, stretching his bow, resolved in his mind to return blow for blow.

sanskrit: rāvaṇadhvajam uddiśya mumoca niśitaṃ śaram mahāsarpam ivāsahyaṃ jvalantaṃ svena tejasā
english: He released a sharp arrow aimed at Rāvaṇa's standard — irresistible as a great serpent, blazing with its own splendour.

sanskrit: jagāma sa mahīṃ bhittvā daśagrīvadhvajaṃ śaraḥ sa nikṛtto 'patad bhūmau rāvaṇasya rathadhvajaḥ
english: That arrow, piercing through, struck the ground; the standard of Rāvaṇa's chariot was severed and fell to the earth.

sanskrit: dhvajasyonmathanaṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇaḥ sumahābalaḥ krodhajenāgninā saṃkhye pradīpta iva cābhavat
english: Seeing his standard smashed, the immensely powerful Rāvaṇa seemed to blaze in battle as if ignited by the fire of his own wrath.

sanskrit: sa roṣavaśam āpannaḥ śaravarṣaṃ mahad vaman rāmasya turagān divyāñ śarair vivyādha rāvaṇaḥ
english: Overcome by fury and discharging a great rain of arrows, Rāvaṇa pierced Rāma's divine horses with his shafts.

sanskrit: te viddhā harayas tasya nāskhalan nāpi babhramuḥ babhūvuḥ svasthahṛdayāḥ padmanālair ivāhatāḥ
english: Those horses of his, though struck, neither stumbled nor swerved; they remained composed at heart, as if struck merely by lotus stalks.

sanskrit: teṣām asaṃbhramaṃ dṛṣṭvā vājināṃ rāvaṇas tadā bhūya eva susaṃkruddhaḥ śaravarṣaṃ mumoca ha
english: Seeing the horses' lack of agitation, Rāvaṇa then grew yet more fiercely enraged and discharged another rain of arrows.

sanskrit: gadāś ca parighāṃś caiva cakrāṇi musalāni ca giriśṛṅgāṇi vṛkṣāṃś ca tathā śūlaparaśvadhān
english: Maces, iron clubs, discuses, pestles, mountain peaks, trees, javelins, and battle-axes —

sanskrit: māyāvihitam etat tu śastravarṣam apātayat sahasraśas tato bāṇān aśrāntahṛdayodyamaḥ
english: — all this storm of weapons conjured by māyā he hurled down; then, with heart and effort unwearied, he loosed arrows by the thousands.

sanskrit: tumulaṃ trāsajananaṃ bhīmaṃ bhīmapratisvanam durdharṣam abhavad yuddhe naikaśastramayaṃ mahat
english: The battle became tumultuous, terror-inspiring, fearful, with fearful reverberations, irresistible — a great conflict composed of many weapons.

sanskrit: vimucya rāghavarathaṃ samantād vānare bale sāyakair antarikṣaṃ ca cakārāśu nirantaram mumoca ca daśagrīvo niḥsaṅgenāntarātmanā
english: Releasing shafts all around at Rāghava's chariot and upon the monkey army, and filling the sky continuously with arrows, the ten-headed one discharged them with an utterly free and unencumbered spirit.

sanskrit: vyāyacchamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā tatparaṃ rāvaṇaṃ raṇe prahasann iva kākutsthaḥ saṃdadhe sāyakāñ śitān
english: Seeing Rāvaṇa straining with such total absorption in the battle, Kākutstha, almost smiling, fitted sharp arrows to his bow.

sanskrit: sa mumoca tato bāṇān raṇe śatasahasraśaḥ tān dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇaś cakre svaśaraiḥ khaṃ nirantaram
english: He then released arrows in the battle by hundreds of thousands; seeing them, Rāvaṇa with his own shafts made the sky into an unbroken mass.

sanskrit: tatas tābhyāṃ prayuktena śaravarṣeṇa bhāsvatā śarabaddham ivābhāti dvitīyaṃ bhāsvad ambaram
english: Then, by the blazing rain of arrows loosed by those two, the sky appeared as a second luminous sky, bound together with shafts.

sanskrit: nānimitto 'bhavad bāṇo nātibhettā na niṣphalaḥ tathā visṛjator bāṇān rāmarāvaṇayor mṛdhe
english: As Rāma and Rāvaṇa thus discharged arrows in battle, not one arrow was released without cause, not one failed to penetrate, not one was without effect.

sanskrit: prāyudhyetām avicchinnam asyantau savyadakṣiṇam cakratus tau śaraughais tu nirucchvāsam ivāmbaram
english: Those two fought without pause, shooting left and right, and with swarms of arrows they made the sky breathless, as it were.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya hayān rāmo hayān rāmasya rāvaṇaḥ jaghnatus tau tadānyonyaṃ kṛtānukṛtakāriṇau
english: Rāma slew Rāvaṇa's horses and Rāvaṇa slew Rāma's horses — the two of them then doing and undoing each other's deeds in turn.

sanskrit: tau tathā yudhyamānau tu samare rāmarāvaṇau dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni vismitenāntarātmanā
english: Rāma and Rāvaṇa thus fighting in battle were beheld by all living beings with wonder in their innermost hearts.

sanskrit: ardayantau tu samare tayos tau syandanottamau parasparavadhe yuktau ghorarūpau babhūvatuḥ
english: As they afflicted each other in battle, those two foremost chariots of theirs, bent on mutual destruction, became terrible in aspect.

sanskrit: maṇḍalāni ca vīthīś ca gatapratyāgatāni ca darśayantau bahuvidhāṃ sūtau sārathyajāṃ gatim
english: Their two charioteers displayed many kinds of charioteer's movement — circles, straight rushes, advances and retreats.

sanskrit: ardayan rāvaṇaṃ rāmo rāghavaṃ cāpi rāvaṇaḥ gativegaṃ samāpannau pravartana nivartane
english: Rāma assailing Rāvaṇa and Rāvaṇa assailing Rāghava, the two of them matched in speed of movement, charging forward and wheeling back.

sanskrit: kṣipatoḥ śarajālāni tayos tau syandanottamau ceratuḥ saṃyugamahīṃ sāsārau jaladāv iva
english: As the two of them hurled webs of arrows, those two foremost chariots roamed the battlefield like two rain-clouds drenching the earth.

sanskrit: darśayitvā tadā tau tu gatiṃ bahuvidhāṃ raṇe parasparasyābhimukhau punar eva ca tasthatuḥ
english: Having displayed many kinds of movement in battle, those two then halted once more facing each other.

sanskrit: dhuraṃ dhureṇa rathayor vaktraṃ vaktreṇa vājinām patākāś ca patākābhiḥ sameyuḥ sthitayos tadā
english: As they stood, the yoke-poles of their chariots met yoke-pole to yoke-pole, the horses' muzzles met muzzle to muzzle, and the banners met banner to banner.

sanskrit: rāvaṇasya tato rāmo dhanurmuktaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ caturbhiś caturo dīptān hayān pratyapasarpayat
english: Then Rāma with four sharp arrows released from his bow drove back Rāvaṇa's four blazing horses.

sanskrit: sa krodhavaśam āpanno hayānām apasarpaṇe mumoca niśitān bāṇān rāghavāya niśācaraḥ
english: Overcome by rage at the turning back of his horses, that rover of the night released sharp arrows against Rāghava.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho balavatā daśagrīveṇa rāghavaḥ jagāma na vikāraṃ ca na cāpi vyathito 'bhavat
english: Though deeply pierced by the mighty ten-headed one, Rāghava underwent no change and was not distressed.

sanskrit: cikṣepa ca punar bāṇān vajrapātasamasvanān sārathiṃ vajrahastasya samuddiśya niśācaraḥ
english: And that night-roamer hurled arrows again, equal in sound to the fall of Indra's thunderbolt, aimed directly at the charioteer of the thunderbolt-wielder.

sanskrit: mātales tu mahāvegāḥ śarīre patitāḥ śarāḥ na sūkṣmam api saṃmohaṃ vyathāṃ vā pradadur yudhi
english: But those arrows of great velocity, falling upon the body of Mātali, produced not even the slightest confusion or distress in battle.

sanskrit: tayā dharṣaṇayā kroddho mātaler na tathātmanaḥ cakāra śarajālena rāghavo vimukhaṃ ripum
english: Angered by that assault — on behalf of Mātali rather than himself — Rāghava turned the enemy back with a net of arrows.

sanskrit: viṃśatiṃ triṃśataṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ mumoca rāghavo vīraḥ sāyakān syandane ripoḥ
english: The heroic Rāghava released twenty, thirty, sixty, then hundreds and thousands of arrows upon the foe's chariot.

sanskrit: gadānāṃ musalānāṃ ca parighāṇāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ śarāṇāṃ puṅkhavātaiś ca kṣubhitāḥ saptasāgarāḥ
english: The seven oceans were agitated by the sounds of maces, pestles, iron clubs, and by the wind from the fletched ends of arrows.

sanskrit: kṣubdhānāṃ sāgarāṇāṃ ca pātālatalavāsinaḥ vyathitāḥ pannagāḥ sarve dānavāś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: By the agitation of the oceans, all the serpents dwelling on the floor of Pātāla were distressed, as were thousands of Dānavas.

sanskrit: cakampe medinī kṛtsnā saśailavanakānanā bhāskaro niṣprabhaś cābhūn na vavau cāpi mārutaḥ
english: The entire earth shook with its mountains, forests, and groves; the sun became without lustre, and the wind did not blow.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ cintām āpedire sarve sakiṃnaramahoragāḥ
english: Then the gods together with the Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the great seers, all together with the Kinnaras and the great serpents, fell into anxious worry.

sanskrit: svasti gobrāhmaṇebhyo 'stu lokās tiṣṭhantu śāśvatāḥ jayatāṃ rāghavaḥ saṃkhye rāvaṇaṃ rākṣaseśvaram
english: "May there be welfare for cows and Brāhmaṇas; may the worlds endure forever; may Rāghava conquer Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas, in battle."

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahābāhū raghūṇāṃ kīrtivardhanaḥ saṃdhāya dhanuṣā rāmaḥ kṣuram āśīviṣopamam rāvaṇasya śiro 'cchindac chrīmaj jvalitakuṇḍalam
english: Then Rāma, the mighty-armed increaser of the glory of the Raghus, fitting to his bow a crescent-bladed arrow like a venomous serpent, severed Rāvaṇa's noble head with its blazing earring.

sanskrit: tac chiraḥ patitaṃ bhūmau dṛṣṭaṃ lokais tribhis tadā tasyaiva sadṛśaṃ cānyad rāvaṇasyotthitaṃ śiraḥ
english: That head fell to the ground and was seen by the three worlds; yet another head, equal to that one, rose up upon Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: tat kṣipraṃ kṣiprahastena rāmeṇa kṣiprakāriṇā dvitīyaṃ rāvaṇaśiraś chinnaṃ saṃyati sāyakaiḥ
english: That too was swiftly severed in battle by Rāma, swift of hand and swift in action — a second head of Rāvaṇa cut off with arrows.

sanskrit: chinnamātraṃ ca tac chīrṣaṃ punar anyat sma dṛśyate tad apy aśanisaṃkāśaiś chinnaṃ rāmeṇa sāyakaiḥ
english: No sooner was that head severed than yet another appeared; that too was cut off by Rāma with arrows like thunderbolts.

sanskrit: evam eva śataṃ chinnaṃ śirasāṃ tulyavarcasām na caiva rāvaṇasyānto dṛśyate jīvitakṣaye
english: In this same way a hundred heads of equal splendour were severed, yet no end was to be seen in the diminishment of Rāvaṇa's life.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāstravid vīraḥ kausalyānandivardhanaḥ mārgaṇair bahubhir yuktaś cintayām āsa rāghavaḥ
english: Then the heroic Rāghava, increaser of Kausalyā's joy, knower of all weapons, laden with many arrows, fell into deep thought.

sanskrit: mārīco nihato yais tu kharo yais tu sudūṣaṇaḥ krañcāraṇye virādhas tu kabandho daṇḍakā vane
english: "Those by which Mārīca was slain, those by which Khara and Sudūṣaṇa were slain, Virādha in the Krañca forest, and Kabandha in the Daṇḍaka forest —"

sanskrit: ta ime sāyakāḥ sarve yuddhe pratyayikā mama kiṃ nu tat kāraṇaṃ yena rāvaṇe mandatejasaḥ
english: "— all those arrows have been my trusted weapons in battle; what then is the reason that they grow feeble against Rāvaṇa?"

sanskrit: iti cintāparaś cāsīd apramattaś ca saṃyuge vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi rāghavo rāvaṇorasi
english: Thus absorbed in thought, yet unrelenting in battle, Rāghava poured rains of arrows upon Rāvaṇa's chest.

sanskrit: rāvaṇo 'pi tataḥ kruddho rathastho rākṣaseśvaraḥ gadāmusalavarṣeṇa rāmaṃ pratyardayad raṇe
english: And Rāvaṇa too, enraged, the lord of the rākṣasas standing in his chariot, afflicted Rāma in battle with a rain of maces and pestles.

sanskrit: devadānavayakṣāṇāṃ piśācoragarakṣasām paśyatāṃ tan mahad yuddhaṃ sarvarātram avartata
english: Before the watching eyes of gods, Dānavas, Yakṣas, Piśācas, serpents, and rākṣasas, that great battle continued through the entire night.

sanskrit: naiva ratriṃ na divasaṃ na muhūrtaṃ na cakṣaṇam rāmarāvaṇayor yuddhaṃ virāmam upagacchati
english: Neither by night nor by day, neither for a moment nor for the twinkling of an eye did the battle between Rāma and Rāvaṇa find any pause.
